hypothesis: A fixed 20% gold sleeve in a QQQ-heavy portfolio reduces realized tail risk more reliably than replacing the same 20% with SPY, without sacrificing more than 3 percentage points of CAGR.

required: Lower daily maximum drawdown than QQQ and QQQ80_SPY20 in both subperiods
Lower 95% daily Expected Shortfall than both in both subperiods
Lower annualized daily volatility than both in both subperiods
CAGR no more than 3 percentage points below QQQ in either subperiod

secondary_research.hypothesis: The same fixed 20% gold sleeve is a consistently superior risk-adjusted-return diversifier to replacing 20% of QQQ with SPY, not merely a tail-risk reducer.

required: QQQ80_GLD20 Sharpe ratio is at least QQQ80_SPY20 in both fixed subperiods
QQQ80_GLD20 maximum drawdown and 95% daily Expected Shortfall are no worse than QQQ80_SPY20 in both fixed subperiods
QQQ80_GLD20 CAGR is no more than 3 percentage points below QQQ in either fixed subperiod

secondary_research.conclusion: Reject the stronger claim that gold is a regime-independent Sharpe enhancer versus a 20% SPY sleeve. The early fixed period has lower Sharpe than QQQ80_SPY20 even though gold still provides materially better drawdown, Expected Shortfall, and volatility protection. Keep the existing USE decision narrowly scoped to tail-risk reduction.

daily_validation.provider_contract: Existing investor2 Yahoo Chart adjusted-close contract from scripts/alphazerobeta_empirical_run.py::download_daily
daily_validation.missing_data_policy: Fail on row-count disagreement, common-date drops, missing adjusted closes, or non-positive values. No interpolation or alternate-feed fallback.

portfolio_contract.rebalancing: monthly fixed weights; rebalance after each month-end close for the next trading day
portfolio_contract.expected_shortfall: mean of the worst ceil(5% * observations) daily portfolio returns

monthly_alpaca_iex_crosscheck.return_type: Monthly close-to-close plus actual Alpaca cash distributions with ex-date in the month; distributions credited to the sleeve and reinvested at monthly rebalance.
monthly_alpaca_iex_crosscheck.finding: The earlier distribution-aware monthly study also passed the same directional tail-risk test: QQQ80_GLD20 reduced volatility, maximum drawdown, and monthly 95% Expected Shortfall versus QQQ and QQQ80_SPY20 in both fixed subperiods.
limitations: Distribution accrual was assigned to ex-date month rather than exact payable-date cash availability.

decision.use: Use a fixed 20% gold sleeve as a reusable tail-risk reducer for QQQ-heavy allocation research. The result passed both pre-registered daily subperiod gates and independently agreed with the prior Alpaca IEX monthly distribution-aware study.
do_not_use: Do not treat gold as an expected-return timing signal.
Do not treat the 20% gold sleeve as a regime-independent Sharpe-ratio improvement over a 20% SPY sleeve; the early fixed period Sharpe is lower despite stronger tail-risk protection.
Do not infer that 20% is globally optimal; this study validates the fixed 20% decision rule against QQQ100 and QQQ80_SPY20 only.

limitations: Yahoo Chart adjusted close is a vendor total-return series, not an exchange-consolidated SIP source.
Taxes and investor-specific account treatment are not modeled.
All assets are evaluated in USD; JPY investor currency translation is a separate capital-allocation question.
